subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should OpenClaw add these three persistent `gateway.security.*` opt-in controls and enforce them at the WebSocket upgrade boundary, rather than keeping Gateway browser/proxy hardening limited to the existing origin-policy paths?
rationale: The implementation is a new security boundary and public configuration surface; correctness of the mechanics does not determine whether these controls, names, and operator tradeoffs are the desired long-term Gateway contract.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow opt-in contract
options.body: Approve the pre-handshake boundary and the three settings, conditional on current-head raw-wire proof for duplicate sensitive-header rejection.

options.title: Narrow to existing policy seams
options.body: Ask for the branch to retain only behavior that can be expressed through the existing Gateway origin/trusted-proxy policy without adding parallel security controls.

options.title: Pause for consolidated gateway policy
options.body: Defer this feature until the open origin-policy work establishes the intended combined configuration model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Approve the pre-handshake boundary and the three settings, conditional on current-head raw-wire proof for duplicate sensitive-header rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion specifically asks this person to decide the gate placement and setting names.
